Chapter 9: Giving Back and Finding a New Purpose
Surviving cancer, and then making it back to the very top of the sport, brought something unexpected—a whole new sense of responsibility.
The journey wasn’t just about personal victory anymore. Suddenly, the story was inspiring millions of people. And with that inspiration came a real chance to give back, to use everything learned and hard-won, for something much bigger than just crossing the finish line first.
That’s when the idea of starting a foundation began to take shape.
Imagine being able to support others who are facing the same fears and unknowns—offering hope, encouragement, and real resources to those fighting for their lives. Of course, it wasn’t easy. There were plenty of logistical headaches, and the emotional demands could feel overwhelming at times.
But here’s the thing—it was also deeply rewarding. It brought a sense of purpose that went far beyond any race result.
Meeting others who were in the middle of their own fight with cancer changed everything. Every single story was unique, every person incredibly courageous. Instead of just giving hope, their determination and honesty became a new source of inspiration.
The foundation turned into more than just an organization—it became a community. Survivors, families, and supporters all coming together, sharing strength, and lifting each other up.
Of course, there were tough moments. Sometimes the needs felt endless, and progress could be painfully slow. It was frustrating, and there were days when it seemed like the challenges might outweigh the victories.
But all those lessons from cycling—and beating illness—made a difference. Persistence, teamwork, and just plain refusing to give up... those things mattered here, too. Every person helped, every story that was heard, was a powerful reminder of why this journey really counted.
You know, giving back has its own kind of healing power.
It turns pain into purpose. It helps you find meaning in the struggle, and it connects you with others in ways that go far beyond sport.
In the end, those victories off the bike—those moments of real compassion and resilience—became just as important as any win on the road.
Each one is proof of the incredible strength we can find, both in ourselves and in each other.
